claims.evidence: This claim is supported by biophysical data in Figure 3D-F showing monomeric UHRF1.

claims.claim: The histone- and DNA-binding domains of UHRF1 interact and general DNA binding releases this physical association.
claims.source: Collectively, these results show that the histone- and DNA-binding domains of UHRF1 interact and that general DNA binding releases this physical association.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by pull-down data in Figure 3A-B showing interaction and its disruption by DNA.

claims.claim: Ligand-induced intramolecular rearrangement of UHRF1 domain connectivity results in high-affinity retention of UHRF1 on chromatin through positive regulation of histone- and DNA-binding activities.
claims.source: The data further suggest that ligand-induced intramolecular rearrangement of UHRF1 domain connectivity results in high-affinity retention of UHRF1 on chromatin through positive regulation of histone- and DNA-binding activities.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined binding and pull-down data showing conformational changes upon ligand binding.

claims.claim: HeDNA enhances histone interaction with UHRF1.
claims.source: However, two key differences between our findings are that we show reciprocal positive allostery between the histone- and DNA-binding domains of UHRF1, and that general DNA interaction (regardless of methylation state) can displace the TTD-PHD domain and enhance histone interaction.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 2A and comparison to prior work (Fang et al., 2016).

claims.claim: General DNA interaction (regardless of methylation state) can displace the TTD-PHD domain and enhance histone interaction.
claims.source: that general DNA interaction (regardless of methylation state) can displace the TTD-PHD domain and enhance histone interaction
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 2A and pull-down data in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Robust ubiquitylation of an H31-32K9me2 peptide was observed in a 20 min end-point assay in the presence of HeDNA.
claims.source: Surprisingly, we observed robust ubiquitylation of an H31-32K9me2 peptide (Supplementary file 1) in a 20 min end-point assay in the presence of HeDNA (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: Neither apo-UHRF1, SyDNA, nor UnDNA could stimulate ubiquitylation activity at concentrations well above their measured Kd values.
claims.source: Neither apo-UHRF1, SyDNA, nor UnDNA could stimulate this activity at concentrations well above their measured Kd values (Figure 4A)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4A showing lack of activity without HeDNA.

claims.claim: Reduced ubiquitylation activity was observed as HeDNA concentration fell below 300 nM.
claims.source: Consistent with our measured Kd for HeDNA (Figure 1B), we observed reduced ubiquitylation activity as HeDNA concentration fell below 300 nM (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4A showing dose-dependent activity.

claims.claim: This is the first demonstration that a DNA-protein interaction, and in particular an epigenetic modification, directly regulates enzymatic activity of an E3 ubiquitin ligase.
claims.source: To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that a DNA-protein interaction, and in particular an epigenetic modification, directly regulates enzymatic activity of an E3 ubiquitin ligase.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on the novelty of the finding and comparison to existing literature on E3 ligase regulation.

claims.claim: HeDNA stimulated a 2.5-fold rate enhancement of UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation compared to UnDNA.
claims.source: We measured a 2.5-fold rate enhancement of UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation in the presence of HeDNA vs. UnDNA, both in the presence or absence of H31-32K9me2 peptide (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by rate measurement data in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: The rate of HeDNA-stimulated H31-32K9me2 mono-ubiquitylation was stimulated by more than 100-fold over the rate obtained with UnDNA.
claims.source: In sharp contrast, the rate of HeDNA-stimulated H31-32K9me2 mono-ubiquitylation was stimulated by more than 100-fold over the rate obtained with UnDNA (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by rate measurement data in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: The rate of auto-ubiquitylation was 20-fold faster than the rate of peptide ubiquitylation in the presence of UnDNA.
claims.source: Comparing the rate of activity on UHRF1 substrates (peptide vs. self), the rate of auto-ubiquitylation was 20-fold faster than the rate of peptide ubiquitylation in the presence of UnDNA.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by rate measurement data in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: The rate of peptide ubiquitylation was seven-fold faster than the rate of auto-ubiquitylation in the presence of HeDNA.
claims.source: Conversely, the rate of peptide ubiquitylation was seven-fold faster than the rate of auto-ubiquitylation in the presence of HeDNA (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by rate measurement data in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: HeDNA-binding acts as an allosteric switch to enhance ubiquitylation of histone substrates.
claims.source: Based on these observations, we propose that HeDNA-binding acts as an allosteric switch to enhance ubiquitylation of histone substrates.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the rate data in Figure 4B showing differential substrate preference with HeDNA.

claims.claim: UHRF1 mono-, di-, and tri-ubiquitylation of purified HeLa mononucleosomes was stimulated by HeDNA.
claims.source: Similar to peptide substrates, UHRF1 mono-, di-, and tri-ubiquitylation of purified HeLa mononucleosomes was stimulated by HeDNA (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: The enhanced ubiquitylation activity of UHRF1 is relevant in the context of chromatin.
claims.source: confirming that the enhanced ubiquitylation activity of UHRF1 is relevant in the context of chromatin
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by mononucleosome ubiquitylation data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Excess H31-15K9me2 peptide effectively inhibited UHRF1 enzymatic activity towards mononucleosome substrates.
claims.source: In addition, when excess H31-15K9me2 peptide (Supplementary file 1) (which harbors the TTD-PHD binding site but not the published ubiquitin target lysines) was added to UHRF1 mononucleosome ubiquitylation assays, H31-15K9me2 effectively inhibited enzymatic activity towards mononucleosome substrates (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4C showing inhibition by competing peptide.

claims.claim: HeDNA concentrations as high as 40 μM did not block mononucleosome ubiquitylation.
claims.source: In contrast, HeDNA concentrations as high as 40 μM did not block mononucleosome ubiquitylation, consistent with its role as an activator of UHRF1 E3 ligase activity.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4C showing no inhibition by HeDNA.

claims.claim: The N-terminus of H3 is the primary binding site for substrate recognition through the TTD-PHD.
claims.source: These results suggest that the N-terminus of H3 is the primary binding site for substrate recognition through the TTD-PHD
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the peptide competition data in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: DNA interaction can occur in trans to the nucleosome being targeted for ubiquitylation.
claims.source: that DNA interaction can occur in trans to the nucleosome being targeted for ubiquitylation
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that excess HeDNA does not inhibit nucleosome ubiquitylation in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: H3mut, Linkermut, DNAmut, and HeDNAmut UHRF1 exhibited defects in HeDNA-dependent H3 ubiquitylation.
claims.source: Characterizing DNA-, HeDNA-, and histone-binding loss-of-function UHRF1 mutants in ubiquitylation assays revealed defects in HeDNA-dependent H3 ubiquitylation, with the exception of the previously reported SRA loss-of-function mutant (D469G) (Avvakumov et al., 2008)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: D469G UHRF1 exhibited wild-type binding to HeDNA.
claims.source: that exhibited wild-type binding to HeDNA in our assays (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: The TTD-PHD is the substrate-binding domain for HeDNA-dependent H3 ubiquitylation.
claims.source: Ubiquitylation defects observed for H3mut and Linkermut confirmed a critical role for the TTD-PHD as the substrate-binding domain for HeDNA-dependent H3 ubiquitylation
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4D showing loss of activity for TTD-PHD mutants.

claims.claim: Multivalent cis engagement of H3K9me3 by the UHRF1 TTD-PHD is required for proper ubiquitylation.
claims.source: demonstrated that multivalent cis engagement of H3K9me3 by the UHRF1 TTD-PHD is required for proper ubiquitylation (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4D showing defects for Linkermut.

claims.claim: DNAmut UHRF1 showed complete loss of HeDNA-dependent ubiquitylation.
claims.source: In addition, complete loss of HeDNA-dependent ubiquitylation for DNAmut UHRF1
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: HeDNAmut UHRF1 showed absence of multi-ubiquitylated H3.
claims.source: the absence of multi-ubiquitylated H3 for HeDNAmut UHRF1 further support the role of DNA binding and HeDNA recognition to fully activate UHRF1 ubiquitin ligase activity
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: Neither ITC nor NMR spectrum intensity loss measurements indicated a change in UHRF1 affinity for E2 conjugates in the absence or presence of HeDNA.
claims.source: Surprisingly, neither ITC nor NMR spectrum intensity loss measurements indicated a change in affinity for the E2 conjugates in the absence or presence of HeDNA (Figure 5A–B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ITC data in Figure 5A and NMR data in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation was readily observed in the presence of HeDNA and UnDNA.
claims.source: In addition, we readily observed UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation in the presence of HeDNA and UnDNA (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), indicating the RING domain of UHRF1 could productively interact with E2-ub regardless of the methylation status of the bound DNA.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Upon UHRF1 binding to the conjugated E2, NMR resonances belonging to the conjugated ubiquitin did not suffer as great a loss in intensity.
claims.source: Notably, upon E3 binding to the conjugated E2, NMR resonances belonging to the conjugated ubiquitin did not suffer as great a loss in intensity (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–C), indicating that ubiquitin retained its dynamics when bound to the E3.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by NMR data in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B-C.

claims.claim: UHRF1 binding does not promote closed E2-ub states as strongly as other canonical RING domain E3's.
claims.source: This observation suggests that UHRF1 binding does not promote closed E2-ub states as strongly as other canonical RING domain E3's (Christensen et al., 2007; Pruneda et al., 2011a, 2012).
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from NMR data in Figure 5B and comparison to prior studies on other E3 ligases.

claims.claim: The rate of ubiquitin discharge from E2 showed only a modest increase in the reactivity of the conjugate in the presence of HeDNA.
claims.source: The rate of ubiquitin discharge from E2 in these assays (monitored by the loss of the E2-ub and the appearance of free E2) showed only a modest increase in the reactivity of the conjugate in the presence of HeDNA (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: HeDNA-dependent activation of UHRF1 RING activity does not occur through enhancement of the intrinsic rate of ubiquitin discharge from the E2 to non-specific lysine sidechains.
claims.source: These results suggest that HeDNA-dependent activation of UHRF1 RING activity does not occur through enhancement of the intrinsic rate of ubiquitin discharge from the E2 to non-specific lysine sidechains.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the modest rate increase in ubiquitin discharge assays in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: When an H31-20 peptide was added to ubiquitin discharge reactions, rapid conversion of E2-ub to E2 was observed.
claims.source: Remarkably, when an H31-20 peptide (Supplementary file 1) was added to ubiquitin discharge reactions, we observed rapid conversion of E2-ub to E2 (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: The appearance of a band corresponding to ubiquitylated H31-20 was observed in ubiquitin discharge reactions with H3 peptide.
claims.source: Additionally, we observed the appearance of a band corresponding to ubiquitylated H31-20 (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: A decrease in the amount of free ubiquitin and UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation was observed when H3 peptide was present in ubiquitin discharge reactions.
claims.source: Notably, we also observed a decrease in the amount of free ubiquitin and UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation formed when peptide was present, presumably because more ubiquitin was being transferred to H3 (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: Even under conditions where free lysine was in great excess, ubiquitin was transferred rapidly and preferentially to H3 substrate in the presence of HeDNA.
claims.source: Thus, even under conditions where free lysine was in great excess, ubiquitin was transferred rapidly and preferentially to H3 substrate in the presence of HeDNA.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5C showing preferential H3 ubiquitylation.

claims.claim: Neither H31-20K14acK18ac nor H31-20K9acK14acK18ac were capable of being modified with ubiquitin.
claims.source: Neither the H31-20K14acK18ac nor H31-20K9acK14acK18ac were capable of being modified with ubiquitin (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5D showing no ubiquitylation of acetylated peptides.

claims.claim: Rapid E2-ub depletion was only observed in the sample containing H31-20 with unblocked lysines.
claims.source: Additionally, rapid E2-ub depletion was only observed in the sample containing H31-20 (Figure 5D), indicating that substrate binding alone does not enhance the E3 ligase activity of UHRF1 in the presence of HeDNA.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5D.

claims.claim: Substrate binding alone does not enhance the E3 ligase activity of UHRF1 in the presence of HeDNA.
claims.source: indicating that substrate binding alone does not enhance the E3 ligase activity of UHRF1 in the presence of HeDNA
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5D showing no enhancement with acetylated peptides.

claims.claim: Reactions that contained unblocked lysines on H31-20 accumulated less auto-ubiquitylated UHRF1 and free ubiquitin compared to assays with no peptide or with acetylated H3 peptides.
claims.source: Consistent with our previous single turnover results (Figure 5C), reactions that contained unblocked lysines on H31-20 accumulated less auto-ubiquitylated UHRF1 and free ubiquitin compared to assays with no peptide or with the acetylated H3 peptides (Figure 5D)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5D.

claims.claim: HeDNA alters the substrate specificity of UHRF1 ubiquitylation.
claims.source: supporting a model where HeDNA alters the substrate specificity of UHRF1 ubiquitylation
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5C-D showing preferential H3 ubiquitylation with HeDNA.

claims.claim: Virtually no ubiquitylated species of H3 were observed in assays that lacked HeDNA.
claims.source: It is worth noting that in all single and multiple turnover assays performed, virtually no ubiquitylated species of H3 were observed in assays that lacked HeDNA.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5C-D.

claims.claim: HeDNA stimulates UHRF1 ubiquitin ligase activity through a novel regulatory mechanism.
claims.source: Taken together, these data demonstrate that HeDNA stimulates UHRF1 ubiquitin ligase activity through a novel regulatory mechanism
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the combined data from Figures 4-5 showing HeDNA-dependent activation distinct from known E3 ligase regulatory mechanisms.

claims.claim: HeDNA binding serves as an allosteric switch that directs the TTD-PHD bound H3 substrate to the E2-ub active site for transfer.
claims.source: suggest that HeDNA binding serves as an allosteric switch that directs the TTD-PHD bound H3 substrate to the E2-ub active site for transfer
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined ubiquitylation and discharge assay data showing HeDNA-dependent substrate preference.

claims.claim: The only histone peptides enriched greater than ten-fold in HeDNA samples relative to UnDNA samples were derived from H3.
claims.source: We first identified peptides that were enriched in the HeDNA sample relative to the UnDNA sample, and the only histone peptides that were enriched greater than ten-fold were derived from H3 (Supplementary file 2)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Supplementary file 2.

claims.claim: Ubiquitin remnants on H3 peptides were heavily enriched in samples reacted in the presence of HeDNA relative to UnDNA.
claims.source: Consistent with our findings that HeDNA stimulates UHRF1 ubiquitin ligase activity, ubiquitin remnants on H3 peptides were heavily enriched in samples reacted in the presence of HeDNA relative to UnDNA (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1,2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1,2.

claims.claim: In addition to H3K18 and H3K23, H3K14ub, H3K27ub, and H3K36ub were heavily enriched in the presence of HeDNA.
claims.source: In addition to the previously identified sites H3K18 and H3K23, we also found H3K14ub, H3K27ub, and H3K36ub heavily enriched in the presence of HeDNA (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1,2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1,2.

claims.claim: Abundant H3K18ub and H3K23ub (multi-ubiquitylation) on the same peptide were identified.
claims.source: We further identified abundant H3K18ub and H3K23ub (multi-ubiquitylation) on the same peptide.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: H3K18ub was the most abundant ubiquitylated peptide based upon spectral counts (greater than 15-fold more than any other site).
claims.source: H3K18ub was the most abundant ubiquitylated peptide based upon spectral counts (greater than 15-fold more than any other site)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: H3K23ub was only observed in the context of H3K18ub.
claims.source: H3K23ub was only observed in the context of H3K18ub (Figure 6B)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: H3K18 is the preferred ubiquitylation site for UHRF1.
claims.source: Collectively these results suggest that H3K18 is the preferred ubiquitylation site for UHRF1
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B showing H3K18ub as the most abundant site.

claims.claim: UHRF1 can target a number of lysines on the H3 tail for ubiquitylation.
claims.source: but that UHRF1 can target a number of lysines on the H3 tail
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B identifying multiple ubiquitylation sites.

claims.claim: Changes to the sites of UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation were observed in the presence of HeDNA.
claims.source: Consistent with our model of HeDNA altering UHRF1 substrate preferences, we also observed changes to the sites of UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation in the presence of HeDNA (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C–E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6—figure supplement 2C-E.

claims.claim: A nine-fold enrichment of UHRF1 K303ub was identified in the presence of HeDNA.
claims.source: In particular, we identified a nine-fold enrichment of UHRF1 K303ub, a solvent exposed lysine in the PHD near the C-terminus of a bound H3 peptide (Figure 6—figure supplement 2D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6—figure supplement 2C-D.

claims.claim: An additional auto-ubiquitylated UHRF1 band was observed in the presence of HeDNA compared to that observed with UnDNA.
claims.source: Accordingly, we observed an additional auto-ubiquitylated UHRF1 band in the presence of HeDNA compared to that observed with UnDNA (Figure 6—figure supplement 2E), corroborating our mass spectrometry results.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblot data in Figure 6—figure supplement 2E.

claims.claim: Several histone PTMs co-occurred with ubiquitylated H3 peptides, including all three states of H3K9 methylation.
claims.source: We also identified several histone PTMs that co-occurred with ubiquitylated H3 peptides, including all three states of H3K9 methylation (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B identifying co-occurring modifications.

claims.claim: Several of the most enriched H3 peptides not containing ubiquitin remnants also contained H3K9me2.
claims.source: Additionally, several of the most enriched H3 peptides not containing ubiquitin remnants also contained H3K9me2 (Supplementary file 2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Supplementary file 2.

claims.claim: Ubiquitylated H3 was detected in the presence of HeDNA (but not UnDNA) on nucleosomes marked with H3K9me3.
claims.source: We confirmed this epigenetic link by immunoblotting HeLa mononucleosomes ubiquitylated by UHRF1. Ubiquitylated H3 was detected in the presence of HeDNA (but not UnDNA) on nucleosomes marked with H3K9me3

claims.claim: Ubiquitylated H3 was not detected on nucleosomes marked with H3K9acK14ac.
claims.source: but not on nucleosomes marked with H3K9acK14ac (Figure 6C)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblot data in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: UHRF1 could modify H2A and H2B at concentrations above 5 μM.
claims.source: In addition, titrating recombinant human histones H3, H2A, and H2B into ubiquitylation assays revealed that while UHRF1 could modify H2A and H2B at concentrations above 5 μM
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: H3 could be modified by UHRF1 at sub-micromolar concentrations.
claims.source: H3 could be modified at sub-micromolar concentrations
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: H3K9me2 protein could be modified by UHRF1 at even lower concentrations than unmodified H3.
claims.source: H3K9me2 protein (synthesized by native chemical ligation) could be modified at even lower concentrations (Figure 6—figure supplement 3)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: H3K9 methylation directs UHRF1 ubiquitylation to adjacent lysine residues in the presence of HeDNA.
claims.source: Taken together, these findings strongly support the role of H3K9 methylation in directing UHRF1 ubiquitylation to adjacent lysine residues in the presence of HeDNA.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry and immunoblot data in Figure 6B-C and Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: Other histone PTMs co-occurring on ubiquitylated peptides were H3K23ac, H3K27me2, H3K36ac, and H3K37me3.
claims.source: Other histone PTMs co-occurring on ubiquitylated peptides were: H3K23ac, also identified in another study (Qin et al., 2015); H3K27me2, which often co-occurs with H3K9me2/me3 and is considered a hallmark of facultative heterochromatin (Boros et al., 2014); H3K36ac, and H3K37me3 (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1,2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1,2, and citations to prior studies.

claims.claim: UHRF1 is targeted to chromatin through its coordinated histone and DNA reading activities.
claims.source: we propose a model where UHRF1 is targeted to chromatin through its coordinated histone and DNA reading activities (Figure 7A)
claims.evidence: This is a model claim synthesizing the binding and chromatin association data from Figures 1-3.

claims.claim: When UHRF1 encounters HeDNA, H3 ubiquitylation serves as a mechanism to facilitate the recruitment of DNMT1 to replicating regions of the genome to copy parental DNA methylation patterns.
claims.source: When UHRF1 encounters HeDNA, H3 ubiquitylation serves as a mechanism to facilitate the recruitment of DNMT1 to replicating regions of the genome to copy parental DNA methylation patterns (Figure 7B).
claims.evidence: This is a model claim synthesizing the ubiquitylation data from Figures 4-6 with prior knowledge of DNMT1 recruitment.

claims.claim: HeDNA sensing is not required to target UHRF1 to bulk chromatin.
claims.source: While it remains to be seen whether uncoupling UHRF1 from HeDNA recognition changes its residence genome-wide, our studies show HeDNA sensing is not required to target UHRF1 to bulk chromatin.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by chromatin association data in Figure 1D showing HeDNAmut binds chromatin.

claims.claim: Coordinated recognition of H3 and DNA, independent of HeDNA discrimination, drives chromatin interaction.
claims.source: Rather, coordinated recognition of H3 and DNA, independent of HeDNA discrimination, drives chromatin interaction.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the binding and chromatin association data in Figures 1-2.

claims.claim: The avidity resulting from sub-μM affinities of UHRF1 for both DNA and H3 peptides through reciprocal positive allostery provides a biochemical basis by which UHRF1 is exclusively localized on chromatin.
claims.source: We propose that the avidity resulting from sub-μM affinities of UHRF1 for both DNA and H3 peptides through reciprocal positive allostery provides a biochemical basis by which UHRF1 is exclusively localized on chromatin.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the binding data in Figures 1-2 showing enhanced affinities with both ligands.

claims.claim: Small perturbations to histone binding affinity through the TTD-PHD dramatically affect chromatin targeting of UHRF1.
claims.source: This may also explain why small perturbations to histone binding affinity through the TTD-PHD (e.g., Linkermut and TTD aromatic cage mutation [Rothbart et al., 2013, 2012]) so dramatically affect chromatin targeting of this protein.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the chromatin association data in Figure 1D and citations to prior studies.

claims.claim: UHRF1 appears to be versatile in targeting lysines for ubiquitylation on the H3 tail.
claims.source: UHRF1 appears to be versatile in targeting lysines for ubiquitylation on the H3 tail (Figure 6B)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B identifying multiple ubiquitylation sites.

claims.claim: UHRF1's ability to target multiple lysines may be related to the complexities of PTM patterning found on the H3 tail and the necessity to promote efficient recruitment of DNMT1 to differentially modified chromatin environments.
claims.source: this ability may be related to the complexities of PTM patterning found on this region of the H3 tail (Young et al., 2009) and the necessity to promote efficient recruitment of DNMT1 to differentially modified chromatin environments
claims.evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the mass spectrometry data and citation to prior work on PTM complexity.

claims.claim: UHRF1 histone ubiquitylation may serve other roles in DNA related processes (i.e., DNA repair).
claims.source: In addition, UHRF1 histone ubiquitylation may serve other roles in DNA related processes (i.e., DNA repair) (Liang et al., 2015; Tian et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is a speculative claim based on citations to prior studies linking UHRF1 to DNA repair.

claims.claim: DNMT1 has an intrinsic preference for HeDNA substrates.
claims.source: Important to note are studies on the enzymology of DNMT1 activity that show the enzyme has an intrinsic preference for HeDNA substrates (Goyal et al., 2006)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior enzymatic studies of DNMT1.

claims.claim: DNMT1 methylates in a processive manner.
claims.source: methylates in a processive manner (Bestor and Ingram, 1983; Hermann et al., 2004)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior enzymatic studies of DNMT1.

claims.claim: UHRF1 functions to provide a nucleation event for DNMT1 recruitment to chromatin.
claims.source: Considering DNMT1 behavior on oligonucleotide substrates, it is intriguing to speculate that UHRF1 functions to provide a nucleation event for DNMT1 recruitment to chromatin.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the combined data and knowledge of DNMT1 processivity.

claims.claim: HeDNA is bound by the UHRF1 SRA in a manner that positions the RING in proximity to the H3 binding region of UHRF1.
claims.source: We speculate that HeDNA is bound by the UHRF1 SRA in a manner that positions the RING in proximity to the H3 binding region of UHRF1.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the ubiquitylation data and structural considerations.

claims.evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the differential ubiquitylation activity with different DNA substrates.

claims.claim: The NKR finger of the UHRF1 SRA adopts a highly ordered conformation upon HeDNA binding.

claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior structural studies.

claims.evidence: This is a speculative claim based on citation to a prior study.

results.result: UHRF1 binds DNA with selectivity for hemi-methylated CpG (HeDNA) over unmethylated (UnDNA) and symmetrically methylated (SyDNA) DNA, with 10-20 fold preference for HeDNA over UnDNA and 5-10 fold preference over SyDNA. Specific mutations (DNAmut and HeDNAmut) selectively disrupt DNA binding or HeDNA sensing.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C10-C13 are directly supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 1B showing differential binding affinities. The salt sensitivity (C14) is supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2. The mutational analysis provides clear structure-function relationships validated by both binding data and structural information.

results.result: HeDNA recognition by UHRF1 is required for DNA methylation maintenance in cells. While wild-type UHRF1 rescues DNA methylation loss in knockdown cells, the HeDNAmut mutant cannot rescue despite retaining DNA binding ability, similar to H3mut, RINGmut, and DNAmut.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C15-C19 are supported by genetic complementation experiments in Figure 1C showing that HeDNAmut fails to rescue 5mC levels despite binding DNA (Figure 1B). The experimental design appropriately uses multiple loss-of-function mutants as controls, and the immunofluorescence quantification shows clear differences between rescue and non-rescue conditions.

results.result: HeDNA recognition is dispensable for UHRF1 chromatin interaction. The HeDNAmut retains chromatin binding ability, suggesting that histone- and DNA-binding domains perform complementary functions for chromatin targeting, while HeDNA recognition provides an additional regulatory layer beyond chromatin localization.
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C20-C22, C109-C110 are supported by chromatin association assays in Figure 1D showing that HeDNAmut binds chromatin similarly to wild-type, while H3mut and DNAmut do not. This dissociation between chromatin binding and functional rescue (from previous result) is logically consistent and well-demonstrated.

results.result: UHRF1 histone- and DNA-binding modules are regulated by reciprocal positive allostery. DNA (regardless of methylation status) enhances histone binding, and H3K9me3 peptides enhance DNA binding 5-10 fold. The enhancement depends on the epigenetic signature on H3 and requires intact TTD-PHD multivalent engagement.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C23, C26-C37, C46-C47 are supported by comprehensive fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 2 showing mutual enhancement of binding when both ligands are present. The mutational analysis (H3mut, Linkermut, DNAmut, HeDNAmut) systematically validates the mechanism. The data demonstrate true reciprocal allostery rather than simple additive effects.

results.result: The UHRF1 TTD-PHD and SRA domains physically interact in an intramolecular manner, and this interaction is disrupted by DNA binding (regardless of methylation status) but not by H3 peptide binding. UHRF1 remains monomeric in the presence and absence of ligands, indicating ligand-induced intramolecular rearrangement.
results.evaluation: Claims C38-C45 are supported by pull-down assays (Figure 3A-C) showing domain interactions and their disruption by DNA, and by multiple biophysical techniques (Figure 3D-F) confirming monomeric state. The combination of pull-down and biophysical data provides strong evidence for intramolecular conformational changes rather than oligomerization.

results.result: HeDNA specifically activates UHRF1 ubiquitin ligase activity toward H3 substrates. HeDNA stimulates H3 ubiquitylation >100-fold compared to UnDNA, while only modestly enhancing auto-ubiquitylation (2.5-fold). Neither SyDNA nor UnDNA can stimulate this activity, and the effect is dose-dependent with HeDNA concentration.
results.evaluation: Claims C48-C56 are supported by ubiquitylation assays in Figure 4A-B showing dramatic HeDNA-specific activation. The rate measurements clearly demonstrate differential substrate preference (peptide vs. self) depending on DNA methylation status. The claim of novelty (C51) regarding DNA-regulated E3 ligase activity is reasonable given the data, though comprehensive literature review would be needed to fully validate this claim.

results.result: HeDNA-stimulated UHRF1 ubiquitylation is relevant in the context of chromatin. UHRF1 ubiquitylates mononucleosomes in a HeDNA-dependent manner, and excess H3 N-terminal peptide (containing TTD-PHD binding site) inhibits nucleosome ubiquitylation while excess HeDNA does not, suggesting the N-terminus is the primary substrate recognition site and DNA can act in trans.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C62 are supported by mononucleosome ubiquitylation assays (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, Figure 4C) showing HeDNA-dependent activity and competitive inhibition by H3 peptide but not by HeDNA. The trans-acting model (C62) is a reasonable inference from the competition data, though direct demonstration would strengthen this claim.

results.result: Multiple UHRF1 domains are required for HeDNA-dependent H3 ubiquitylation. H3mut, Linkermut, DNAmut, and HeDNAmut all show defects in HeDNA-dependent ubiquitylation, confirming that the TTD-PHD is the substrate-binding domain and that multivalent H3K9me3 engagement is required. The D469G mutant retains wild-type activity despite prior reports.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C68 are supported by ubiquitylation assays with mutants in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C. The systematic mutational analysis validates the requirement for each domain. The D469G result (C64) contradicts prior literature but is supported by the authors' binding data (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D), suggesting potential differences in assay conditions.

results.result: HeDNA does not activate UHRF1 by modulating E2-ubiquitin conjugate binding or by enhancing intrinsic ubiquitin discharge rates to non-specific lysines. ITC and NMR show no change in E2-ub affinity with HeDNA, and ubiquitin discharge assays show only modest rate increases with HeDNA in the absence of H3 substrate.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C74 are supported by ITC (Figure 5A), NMR (Figure 5B), and ubiquitin discharge assays (Figure 5C). The data effectively rule out two common E3 ligase activation mechanisms. The NMR analysis showing retained ubiquitin dynamics (C71-C72) provides mechanistic insight, though the inference about closed E2-ub states could benefit from additional structural validation.

results.result: HeDNA alters UHRF1 substrate specificity rather than general catalytic activity. In the presence of HeDNA and H3 peptide, ubiquitin is rapidly and preferentially transferred to H3 even in the presence of excess free lysine. Acetylated H3 peptides that bind TTD-PHD but lack free lysines do not enhance activity, indicating substrate binding alone is insufficient.
results.evaluation: Claims C75-C86 are supported by ubiquitin discharge assays in Figure 5C-D showing preferential H3 ubiquitylation with HeDNA and demonstrating that substrate binding without available lysines does not activate the enzyme. The experiments effectively distinguish between substrate recruitment and catalytic activation. The allosteric switch model (C86) is well-supported by the data.

results.result: Mass spectrometry analysis of UHRF1-ubiquitylated mononucleosomes reveals that H3 is the primary target, with multiple lysines ubiquitylated in a HeDNA-dependent manner. H3K18ub is the most abundant site (>15-fold more than others), H3K23ub only occurs with H3K18ub, and additional sites include H3K14, H3K27, and H3K36.
results.evaluation: Claims C87-C94 are supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B and supplementary figures showing HeDNA-dependent enrichment of ubiquitylated H3 peptides. The quantification by spectral counts provides clear evidence for site preference. The identification of multiple sites beyond the previously known H3K18 and H3K23 is well-documented with appropriate MS/MS validation.

results.result: HeDNA alters UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation site specificity. A nine-fold enrichment of K303 ubiquitylation (in the PHD near bound H3 peptide) was observed with HeDNA, and an additional auto-ubiquitylated band appears on immunoblots with HeDNA compared to UnDNA.
results.evaluation: Claims C95-C97 are supported by mass spectrometry data (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C-E) showing differential auto-ubiquitylation sites and immunoblot validation. The identification of K303 as a HeDNA-enriched site is consistent with the proposed model of RING positioning. The data support the substrate specificity change model.

results.result: H3K9 methylation directs UHRF1 ubiquitylation to adjacent lysines in the presence of HeDNA. Mass spectrometry shows co-occurrence of H3K9me1/2/3 with ubiquitylation, immunoblots confirm ubiquitylation on H3K9me3-marked nucleosomes but not H3K9ac/K14ac nucleosomes, and titration experiments show H3K9me2 is modified at lower concentrations than unmodified H3.
results.evaluation: Claims C98-C105 are supported by mass spectrometry (Figure 6B, Supplementary file 2), immunoblots (Figure 6C), and histone titration experiments (Figure 6—figure supplement 3). The multiple lines of evidence consistently demonstrate the role of H3K9 methylation in directing ubiquitylation. The data effectively link the reader function (H3K9me recognition) to the writer function (ubiquitylation).

results.result: Other histone PTMs co-occur with ubiquitylated H3 peptides, including H3K23ac, H3K27me2, H3K36ac, and H3K37me3.
results.evaluation: Claim C106 is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B identifying these co-occurring modifications. However, the authors appropriately note that the biological significance of these combinations requires future investigation. The identification is descriptive and well-documented.

results.result: Model: UHRF1 is targeted to chromatin through coordinated histone and DNA reading, and when it encounters HeDNA, H3 ubiquitylation facilitates DNMT1 recruitment for DNA methylation inheritance. The avidity from sub-μM affinities through reciprocal allostery provides the biochemical basis for chromatin localization.
results.evaluation: Claims C107-C108, C111-C112 represent the authors' integrative model synthesizing the binding, chromatin association, and ubiquitylation data. The model is well-supported by the experimental results presented in the manuscript. The mechanistic connection to DNMT1 recruitment (C108) relies on prior literature citations, which is appropriate for a model/discussion claim.

results.result: UHRF1 is versatile in targeting multiple lysines on the H3 tail for ubiquitylation, which may relate to PTM complexity and the need to recruit DNMT1 to differentially modified chromatin environments.
results.evaluation: Claim C113 is directly supported by the mass spectrometry data showing multiple ubiquitylation sites. Claim C114 is speculative but reasonable given the data and cited literature on PTM complexity. The speculation is appropriately qualified and represents a plausible biological interpretation.

results.result: Background claims establishing UHRF1's known functions: UHRF1 is a histone- and DNA-binding RING E3 ubiquitin ligase that plays a central role in DNMT1-directed DNA methylation maintenance, recognizes H3K9me2/me3 through its TTD-PHD, and catalyzes H3K18/K23 ubiquitylation.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C7-C9 are background claims supported by citations to prior literature. These establish the context for the current study and are appropriately referenced. These are not novel findings of this manuscript but necessary context.

results.result: DNMT1 has intrinsic preference for HeDNA substrates and methylates processively. The authors speculate that UHRF1 may provide a nucleation event for DNMT1 recruitment to chromatin.
results.evaluation: Claims C116-C117 are supported by citations to prior enzymatic studies of DNMT1. Claim C118 is explicitly speculative and appropriately qualified. The speculation is reasonable given the combined properties of UHRF1 and DNMT1, though it requires future experimental validation.

results.result: Mechanistic speculation: HeDNA binding may position the RING domain in proximity to the H3 binding region, with RING activity potentially restricted when binding SyDNA or UnDNA. Structural studies show the SRA can adopt different conformations with different DNA substrates, and the NKR finger adopts an ordered conformation upon HeDNA binding.
results.evaluation: Claims C119-C120 are explicitly speculative (C123 states "we hypothesize") and lack direct structural evidence for the proposed RING positioning. Claims C121-C122 cite prior structural studies on mouse UHRF1 SRA, which provide supporting context but do not directly demonstrate the proposed mechanism for full-length human UHRF1. The speculation is reasonable but requires structural validation of the active conformation.

results.result: Discussion of potential deubiquitylase: H2BK123ub has a short half-life (~1 minute) in yeast. USP7 may remove H3 ubiquitylation through interaction with DNMT1 and UHRF1, and has been linked to DNA replication and heterochromatin maintenance, but direct evidence of USP7-catalyzed H3 deubiquitylation is lacking.
results.evaluation: Claims C124, C126-C127 are supported by citations to prior studies. Claims C125 and C128 appropriately note the speculative nature and lack of direct evidence. This represents a reasonable discussion of future directions based on existing literature, with appropriate caveats about what remains to be demonstrated.

results.result: UHRF1 histone ubiquitylation may serve roles in other DNA-related processes such as DNA repair.
results.evaluation: Claim C115 is speculative but supported by citations to prior studies linking UHRF1 to DNA repair. This represents appropriate discussion of broader implications beyond the specific focus of the manuscript.

results.result: HeDNA recognition is required for DNA methylation maintenance but is dispensable for chromatin binding. The authors show that HeDNAmut UHRF1 cannot rescue DNA methylation loss in cells (similar to H3mut, RINGmut, and DNAmut), yet HeDNAmut retains chromatin binding ability, suggesting HeDNA recognition provides an additional regulatory layer beyond chromatin targeting.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly acknowledge this finding, stating 'they show that while HeDNA discrimination mutants of UHRF1 are unable to sustain methylation in vivo, they are able to associated with chromatin.' This result is central to the paper's novelty and is not questioned.

results.result: UHRF1 histone- and DNA-binding domains exhibit reciprocal positive allostery. The authors demonstrate that DNA (HeDNA, SyDNA, UnDNA) enhances UHRF1 binding to H3K9me3 peptides, and reciprocally, H3K9me3 peptide enhances DNA binding 5-10 fold irrespective of DNA methylation status. This cooperativity is dependent on the epigenetic signature on H3 and requires intact TTD-PHD multivalent engagement.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly state 'they provide evidence for positive allostery, showing that UHRF1 association with H3 is promoted by the presence of (He)DNA and visa versa.' The reviewers note this as a key difference from Fang et al., acknowledging 'reciprocal positive allostery between the histone- and DNA-binding domains of UHRF1' as a novel contribution.

results.result: DNA binding releases an intramolecular interaction between UHRF1 TTD-PHD and SRA-RING domains. Pull-down experiments show TTD-PHD associates with SRA-RING, and this interaction is disrupted by DNA (regardless of methylation status) but not by H3K9me2 peptide. The authors propose ligand-induced intramolecular rearrangement results in high-affinity chromatin retention through positive regulation of binding activities.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge this mechanism, stating 'They provide a mechanism for this positive allostery, showing that the SRA and TTD-PHD domains normally associate with each other but that his interaction is abrogated in the presence of DNA, which presumably allows the free TTD-PHD domain to associate with its known chromatin target, H3K9me3.' This is accepted as part of the allosteric mechanism.

results.result: HeDNA specifically activates UHRF1 ubiquitylation of H3 substrates. The authors show robust H3 peptide ubiquitylation in the presence of HeDNA but not with SyDNA, UnDNA, or apo-UHRF1. HeDNA stimulated >100-fold rate enhancement of H3 mono-ubiquitylation compared to UnDNA, while auto-ubiquitylation showed only 2.5-fold enhancement. This substrate preference switch is also observed with mononucleosomes.
results.evaluation: Reviewers state 'they provide compelling evidence that the presence HeDNA stimulates the ubiquitylation activity of UHRF1 on H3 substrate' and acknowledge this as a major novel finding. The reviewers note this demonstrates 'HeDNA is an allosteric activator of UHRF1 expanding its lysine targets in histone H3' and represents sufficient novel insight 'particularly regarding ubiquitylation.'

results.result: HeDNA-dependent H3 ubiquitylation requires TTD-PHD substrate binding and multivalent H3K9me3 engagement. Excess H31-15K9me2 peptide (containing TTD-PHD binding site but not ubiquitin target lysines) inhibits mononucleosome ubiquitylation, while excess HeDNA does not. H3mut, Linkermut, DNAmut, and HeDNAmut all show defects in HeDNA-dependent H3 ubiquitylation.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these mechanistic details as part of the overall ubiquitylation activation story. The data supporting TTD-PHD's role in substrate recognition and the requirement for multivalent engagement are not questioned and support the main finding of HeDNA-dependent activation.

results.result: HeDNA activation does not occur through enhanced E2-ub binding or intrinsic discharge rate, but rather through altered substrate specificity. ITC and NMR show no change in E2-ub affinity with HeDNA. Ubiquitin discharge assays show only modest rate increase with HeDNA alone, but rapid H3 ubiquitylation when H3 peptide is present. The authors propose HeDNA serves as an allosteric switch directing TTD-PHD-bound H3 substrate to the E2-ub active site.
results.evaluation: This is the 'lysine prioritization' model that reviewers explicitly challenge as the 'weakest part of the manuscript.' Reviewer states: 'Looking at Figure 5D, I am not convinced that the presence of free lysine preferentially affects auto-ub over H3 peptide' and notes 'there is no prioritization of H3 lysines whatsoever.' The reviewer requests this line of argument be removed unless considerably improved evidence is provided. The mechanism of HeDNA activation remains incompletely explained.

results.result: Mass spectrometry identifies multiple H3 ubiquitylation sites enriched with HeDNA. In addition to H3K18 and H3K23, the authors identify H3K14ub, H3K27ub, and H3K36ub heavily enriched with HeDNA. H3K18ub is the most abundant site (>15-fold more than others), and H3K23ub only occurs with H3K18ub. HeDNA also alters UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation sites, including 9-fold enrichment of K303ub.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the mass spectrometry work as part of the comprehensive analysis, stating the authors 'use mass spectroscopy techniques to determine the PTMs associated with HeDNA simulated UHRF1 activity on nucleosomes.' This identification of multiple ubiquitylation sites is accepted as supporting the allosteric activation model.

results.result: H3K9 methylation directs UHRF1 ubiquitylation to adjacent lysines in the presence of HeDNA. Mass spectrometry shows all three H3K9 methylation states co-occur with ubiquitylated peptides. Immunoblotting confirms ubiquitylated H3 is detected with HeDNA on H3K9me3-marked nucleosomes but not on H3K9acK14ac-marked nucleosomes. Titration experiments show H3K9me2 protein is modified at lower concentrations than unmodified H3.
results.evaluation: Reviewers describe this as 'a detailed biochemical and proteomic analysis of the role of H3K9me3 and hemi-methylated DNA on the functions of the UHRF1 ubiquitin ligase.' The connection between H3K9 methylation and ubiquitylation targeting is accepted as part of the comprehensive characterization.

results.result: Model: UHRF1 is targeted to chromatin through coordinated histone and DNA reading activities via reciprocal positive allostery, and HeDNA recognition activates H3 ubiquitylation to recruit DNMT1. HeDNA sensing is not required for bulk chromatin targeting but provides regulatory specificity. The avidity from sub-μM affinities for both DNA and H3 through positive allostery provides the biochemical basis for exclusive chromatin localization.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly endorse the conceptual advance: 'In general the chromatin field considers protein interactions with epigenetic marks to be the basis for recruitment of chromatin modifiers. This study clearly indicates allosteric activation of chromatin modifiers needs to also be considered.' The model integrating chromatin targeting and allosteric activation is accepted.

results.result: Proposed structural mechanism: HeDNA binding positions the RING in proximity to H3 binding region, while SyDNA/UnDNA binding conformationally restricts RING activity. The NKR finger adopts a highly ordered conformation upon HeDNA binding, which may be critical for H3 ubiquitylation activation.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 states: 'In my view the most important aspect of this paper is to establish the mechanism through which HeDNA binding stimulates ubiquitylation' but notes 'we are left, somewhat disappointingly, with the speculation that HeDNA binding causes specific conformational changes that reposition the RING domain.' The structural mechanism remains speculative and incompletely resolved.
